newsitem.title: CHILE: El Teniente, unions meet Wednesday for wage talks.
newsitem.headline: El Teniente, unions meet Wednesday for wage talks.

text.p: Unions and management at Codelco's 340,000-tonne-a-year El Teniente copper mine will meet Wednesday to try to move forward on wage contract talks, mine and union officials said.

The current contract won't expire until December 31 so there is no talk of strikes yet but talks have been moving slowly, they said at the mine, Codelco's second largest and only mainly underground mine.

"Strikes or demonstrations would be pointless now. At least I haven't heard any of the workers calling for warning strikes or anything like that," said Hugo Allan, president of one of the six unions negotiating with El Teniente management.

The two sides gave sharply different impressions of the atmosphere at talks. Allan said the talks were "complicated" and that he was not optimistic a solution was near, while an El Teniente spokesman said the two sides could reach a solution as early as Friday.
"There is no problem and a good will on both sides for reaching an agreement," said the spokesman for El Teniente.

The main difference was on the length of the new contract and the size of a bonus to be paid upon signing. El Teniente management insists on a four-year contract with a bonus of one million pesos ($2400), while the unions want a maximum three years contract and a larger bonus, both sides said.
Management has already agreed to a wage increase over inflation, but the size of it is still up for negotiation, they said.
Unions are demanding that higher productivity rates at the mine be translated into higher wage increases.

"The point is we've had spectacular productivity increases andthe workers want to share in the benefits of that. Of course, if we share too much of it than the increases in productivity cease to be so spectacular," said Allan.
Management will meet with a committee of leaders of all six unions on Wednesday.
